progression: Year one has 60 EC in Arabic, regional history, politics, religion, academic debates, writing and one faculty-wide choice. The July 2026 regulations apply from 1 September 2026. Transitional Arabic offerings explicitly restricted to earlier cohorts are not part of this example.

Year two adds 30 EC in regional culture, politics, history and Advanced Arabic, followed by the standard 30 EC semester in Cairo or Rabat. Advanced Arabic requires both earlier Arabic courses. Study abroad requires at least 45 first-year EC and Advanced Arabic. Completing the scheduled first-year and prior second-year work satisfies those thresholds. The programme page allows exceptional deviations from study abroad.

Year three contains a 30 EC minor, a second 10 EC faculty-wide choice, two 5 EC regional courses and a 10 EC thesis. The thesis requires all 60 first-year credits and is normally in the final semester. Minor and faculty choice spaces remain restricted as published.
